item.title: Training China's workforce for jobs that barely existed a few years ago
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
SHANGHAI, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- A full-size metro carriage has been moved into the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai, the venue for the 48th WorldSkills Competition -- not for display, but for hands-on competition in rail vehicle technology, one of seven skills making a debut this year. Competitors in this subject are expected to have the mix of skills required by a modern rail network, including an understanding of high-voltage electrical equipment, braking systems, air conditioning, doors and wheelsets, while diagnosing faults and carrying out maintenance. Rail vehicle technology is joined by unmanned aerial systems, intelligent security technology, software testing, digital interactive media design, dental prosthetics technology and retail. The seven newcomers, unveiled as 64 competitions got underway in Shanghai this week, span advanced manufacturing, digital industries, healthcare and modern services. The additions reflect how occupations themselves are changing. The first competition, held in Spain in 1950, focused largely on traditional trades such as construction and manufacturing, while automation, the expansion of the service sector and the rise of the internet later brought new skills onto the competition floor. "Doing a trade in the 1960s and doing the same trade today are not exactly the same," President of WorldSkills International Francis Hourant told reporters on Tuesday, adding that the competition adjusts its portfolio to stay connected with "the reality of the industry." China is trying to make its training system move with those changes. In July, the Ministry of Education added 27 programs to the country's vocational education catalogue, targeting areas including the digital economy, low-altitude economy, advanced equipment and emerging services. The skills behind that shift are already on display at WorldSkills. On Wednesday, pairs of competitors assembled their robots piece by piece. From Thursday, the machines had to prove themselves on the competition floor -- finding their way through maze-like courses, locating objects and completing tasks under the clock. Zeng Zhiwei, a Chinese coach for autonomous mobile robotics, recalled that earlier versions of the event still involved remote-controlled movement. As LiDAR and autonomous navigation spread, the competition changed too. "The competition follows the industry," he said. In another hall, competitors in the new software testing event, a key skill in the digital economy, tapped away at their keyboards, searching for bugs and checking whether systems worked as intended. Software testers help ensure products work reliably before they reach users, a role that has grown as software becomes embedded in fields such as transport, finance and education. Statistics showed that China's digital economy has grown to more than 50 trillion yuan (7.41 trillion U.S. dollars), while the country's digital talent gap remained close to 30 million in 2025. That gap is already reshaping vocational education. In April, 64 technical colleges in Jiangsu Province added 157 programs, about 42 percent of them related to artificial intelligence. In May, 12 technical colleges in Chongqing announced 23 new programs, among them service robot application and maintenance and intelligent connected vehicle technology. However, officials still warned of a growing time lag between industrial change and talent development, as training skilled workers can take three to four years, while emerging industries may evolve much faster. "Technology is changing too fast. If we rush to establish a new program, it may change again very soon," said Zhang Rui, deputy director of the engineering training center at Tianjin University of Technology and Education. "So we start with microprograms." Rather than enrolling a full cohort, these programs start small, with selected students in experimental classes and pilot training. They allow schools to test new content before deciding whether it is ready to be expanded into a broader program. Zhang recalled that companies had once turned often to universities for technical expertise. "Now it is the other way around," she said. "We need to send teachers to companies regularly to learn and keep up with new technologies." At Zhang's university, an industry college works with companies to bring industrial practices into training. Students can work on a smart production-line platform that mirrors an industrial workflow: a customized order placed through an app enters a manufacturing execution system before moving through processes such as material handling, robotic assembly, laser engraving and warehousing. A similar approach combining industry and education can be found elsewhere. At Jiangxi Software Vocational and Technical University, the campus is integrated with an industrial park, with nearly 100 companies involved in tailored training. Enterprise engineers teach classes, while real commercial projects are brought onto campus. So far, more than 20 provincial-level regions in China have developed over 300 industry-education-assessment skills networks, with enterprises taking a leading role in training and skills evaluation. That industry-training link is especially visible in emerging fields such as unmanned aerial systems, where fast-changing commercial applications are creating demand for workers with both hardware and software skills. At the competition in Shanghai, spectators crowd around the arena as competitors piece together drones from roughly 200 components, program them and make final adjustments. Only after the assembly, programming and testing are complete does the aircraft leave the workbench and rise into the air on its own -- a glimpse of a new kind of skilled work that barely had a name only a few years ago. ■

item.title: China, U.S. agree on constructive strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan have a chat over tea with U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The consensus was reached during a tea chat at the White House attended by Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, and Trump and his wife, Melania Trump. Xi said the trip to Washington was his first state visit to the United States in 11 years. During the visit, the two sides added new substance to the vision for the China-U.S. relationship, and agreed to jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Xi said. The two sides also achieved mutually beneficial outcomes in the economic and trade fields, which will be welcomed by the people of both countries and the international community, he added. Stressing that the future of China-U.S. relations is bright, Xi said that it reflects the trend of history. The road to a bright future is often winding, with difficulties and challenges bound to arise along the way, Xi said, adding that it is in line with the laws governing the development of things. Xi said he is willing to work with Trump to write a new chapter in the history of China-U.S. relations with the courage and a sense of responsibility to history. Calling Xi's state visit to the United States constructive and very successful, Trump said that the two sides held in-depth exchanges on U.S.-China relations and major international and regional issues, achieving positive outcomes that will benefit both countries. He said he looks forward to maintaining close contact with Xi and jointly guiding the development of U.S.-China relations. After the tea chat, Xi and Peng, accompanied by Trump and Melania, visited the U.S. National Archives. They walked together into the central hall, where they were briefed on the National Archives and its exhibits. The archives carry the wisdom of the forebears and offer insights for the future, Xi said, adding that over the past 250 years, the American people have pursued the American Dream and built a prosperous country and a beautiful home on the North American continent. The Chinese people, inheriting 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, have continued to make new achievements on the new journey toward realizing the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. As two distinctive countries, China and the United States have different histories and cultures, social systems and development paths, Xi said. However, the people of the two countries share the same aspiration for a better life despite the differences, he said. If the two countries recognize and respect their differences, deepen mutual understanding and learn from each other, seek the biggest common denominator, expand the list of areas for cooperation, and properly manage differences, China-U.S. relations will enjoy steady and sustained growth, Xi said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, together with U.S. President Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump, pose for a group photo at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 25, 2026. item.title: Zooming in on WorldSkills -- How China is reshaping skills in an age of AI, automation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
SHANGHAI, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- In the foyer of the WorldSkills Conference in Shanghai in east China, several overseas participants gathered around a robot, curious to see how it would handle an unusual request, namely marriage advice. When a male participant asked what to do if his wife talked too much, the robot suggested a "three-second rule" before responding. The exchange drew laughter, with one participant joking that it could make a decent marriage counselor. This light-hearted exchange touched on a broader question being discussed at this year's WorldSkills Competition in Shanghai: which skills are difficult for AI to replace, and what new capabilities will people need in an age of AI? WHAT AI CAN'T REPLACE At the digital interactive media design venue, contestants move from product planning to image processing, video production and interaction design during more than 20 hours of competition. Notably, even as AI begins to take over some basic work in the industry, the training remains highly demanding. Zhou Jiaxiang, a member of China's national training squad, described a six-hour video-production module in which contestants may have to adjust dozens or even hundreds of parameters, fine-tune transitions frame by frame and repeatedly render the footage. AI can generate some visual effects within seconds, Zhou said, but the output is often not ready for delivery. Text, a character's gaze, fingers or facial movements may still contain visible flaws, requiring professionals to identify the problem, give precise instructions for revision, and further process the results with conventional software. A professional designer, as Kuang Ying, a professor at East China Normal University's Faculty of Education, put it, can "train AI like a doctoral student," using expertise and judgment to push it toward better results. She said the judgment and aesthetic sense of highly skilled designers remain difficult to replicate. The same question extends beyond creative work. At the retail competition, contestants first build up a store setting, arranging merchandise and visual displays before moving on to face-to-face sales and simulated after-sales complaints. This event also tests online livestreaming and staff training. Beyond the competition arena, AI is already gaining ground in retail. During the first four hours of this year's "618" shopping festival, the number of merchants using JD.com's AI-powered digital hosts for livestreaming surged sixfold year on year, generating more than 70 million yuan (10.37 million U.S. dollars) in sales, according to the company. Yet Lu Chunhua, the venue manager for the WorldSkills retail competition, said: "The core competitiveness of retail is providing emotional value and touching people. That is something AI cannot replace." ONE SPECIALTY, MULTIPLE CAPABILITIES AI's impact, experts said, is not limited to taking over parts of existing work. It is also raising demand for workers who can combine a core specialty with digital and cross-disciplinary skills. At the Industry 4.0 competition, contestants worked to integrate production equipment and other manufacturing resources into a unified system. The project simulates the operation of a smart factory, requiring skills ranging from mechanical assembly and electrical wiring to PLC programming, data collection and analysis, and production scheduling optimization. "Skilled workers in the new era need 'one specialty plus multiple capabilities,'" said Zhang Rui, deputy director of the engineering training center at Tianjin University of Technology and Education in north China. She added that workers who can use digital tools, work across disciplines, and think innovatively are likely to be increasingly sought after. This shift is also reshaping what counts as expertise in software. At the Web Technologies competition, contestants are expected to do more than write code -- they have to understand client needs, design solutions, build databases and programs, and test and debug the final product. Wu Yingxiang, a technical expert and coach for the Chinese team in WorldSkills Web Technologies, said AI is making code generation much faster, pushing programmers toward broader roles. "Every programmer may now become a project manager and a product manager," he said. Data shows that demand for AI-related skills has risen rapidly in China in recent years. Newly posted campus-recruitment positions in AI increased 47.3 percent year on year in the first five months of 2026, according to data from the talent research arm of Maimai, a Chinese networking and recruitment platform. Over the past five years, more than 20 newly recognized occupations have been closely related to AI, with over 40 percent directly linked to future industries. China is moving quickly to address the emerging talent gap. In April, five government departments, including the Ministry of Education, issued an "AI Plus Education" action plan, with measures including upgrading traditional vocational programs, developing new curricula and training systems, and strengthening school-company cooperation for emerging AI-related jobs. The ministry added 27 programs to the country's vocational education catalog in July, covering fields like the digital economy, AI, the low-altitude economy and advanced equipment, with new offerings related to humanoid robots. Schools are adjusting their programs accordingly. Ge Rui, principal of Shanghai Information Technology College, said the college is planning to reshape its professional clusters around areas including AI and industrial digitalization during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), in response to Shanghai's evolving industrial landscape. As training changes, the question is no longer whether workers will use AI, but how they will work with it. Francis Hourant, president of WorldSkills International, said that adapting to the changes in the future is not an either-or choice between humans and AI. "It is not AI in the end. It is the combination of humans and AI," he explained. Asked what young people need most to keep pace with this change, Hourant gave a short but telling answer: "Lifelong learning." ■

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to high-level dialogue marking 5th anniversary of GDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) held at the UN headquarters in New York on Friday. Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind, Xi said. Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted. Xi pointed out that nowadays, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and people in all countries are more keen about development. As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said. ■

item.title: Volume I of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership" presented at Jordan book fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
AMMAN, Sept. 25 (Xinhua) -- A promotional event for the first volume of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership," compiled by Xinhua News Agency, was held on Thursday at the 25th Amman International Book Fair in Jordan's capital. Jamal Dmour, head of the Jordanian-Chinese Friendship Society, introduced the new book to the audience at the event, saying that China's remarkable development experience offers valuable insights for the advancement of humanity. Speaking at the event, Gong Anmin, the charge d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Jordan, said the first volume offers a panoramic media perspective on China's development since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC), documenting the practice of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core in advancing the cause of building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation. Gong said the book provides an important window for the world to explore the keys to China's success in pursuing Chinese modernization. The first volume of "China's Governance Under Xi Jinping's Leadership" contains 26 feature stories and 41 news photographs by Xinhua, offering a vivid, multimedia account of the great practice of China advancing under the leadership of Xi, and fully demonstrating the powerful truth and practical force of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The 25th Amman International Book Fair attracted more than 400 publishing houses from over 20 countries. ■
